FactionStance.description:
One faction's relation to another, dated to the scene where it took this shape.

Dated for the same reason a relationship valence is: a stance stated once is a fact about
the setting, while a stance with a scene attached is a fact about the story, and only the
second can change later without becoming a contradiction.

faction.description: The other faction this stance is directed at.
faction.title: Faction

since.description: Scene from which the stance holds; `None` when it predates page one.
since.title: Since

stance.description: What this faction is to that one: allied, at war, dependent, infiltrated.
stance.title: Stance

FactionStance.title: FactionStance

description:
DR-01, DR-02, DR-10. One collective agent: `canon/factions/<id>.md`.

A faction exists so that pressure on the characters has an origin and a direction. The
split between `wants` and `actual_goal` is what makes it usable: a faction whose stated
goal is its real one can only ever do what it says, and nothing it does can surprise.

**Failure mode** (`definitions.md` Faction): monolithic factions. With no internal dissent
they generate no scenes, only geopolitical scenery - there is nobody inside to disagree
with, so every encounter with them is an encounter with a weather system. `register` is
where the internal texture starts, and it feeds the lexicon: a term's `used_by` is what
keeps that jargon in this faction's mouths and out of everyone else's.

actual_goal.description: What it is actually after. The gap between this and `wants` is where its scenes come from; equal to `wants` only for a faction that never lies.
actual_goal.title: Actual Goal

body.description: The Markdown body, including the internal dissent that keeps the faction from being scenery.
body.title: Body

id.description: Stable identifier; the file is named after it and the index keys a row on it.
id.title: Id

register.description: How its members speak; feeds the lexicon and the voice profiles.
register.title: Register

resources.description: What it can mobilise, and how fast. A threat with no stated reach can be neither escaped nor outrun in any checkable way.
resources.title: Resources

stance.description: Relations to other factions, each dated to the scene it holds from.
stance.title: Stance

wants.description: The stated goal: what it says in public it is trying to achieve.
wants.title: Wants
